title: Unity Event Methods Deep Dive
description: Master Start, Update, Awake, FixedUpdate, LateUpdate, and how they interact with your game loop.

slides.title: The MonoBehaviour Magic ✨
slides.content:
# Built-in Methods

Unity automatically calls certain methods on your scripts if you define them. You've already used `Start()` and `Update()`. There are many more, forming the **MonoBehaviour lifecycle**.

- These methods are **not** overrides (no `override` keyword); Unity finds them by reflection.
- They are called at specific moments: when the object is created, every frame, when physics updates, etc.

Today we'll explore the most important ones beyond Start and Update.

slides.title: Awake() 🌅
slides.content:
# Before Start

`Awake()` is called when the script instance is being loaded. It runs **before** `Start()`, and even if the script is disabled.

- Use `Awake()` to set up references **within the same object** (e.g., `GetComponent<Renderer>()`).
- Use `Start()` for communication between objects (since all Awakes have run).

```csharp
void Awake()
{
    // Get components, initialize internal state
}
```

Order: `Awake()` → `OnEnable()` → `Start()`

quizData.question: When should you use Awake instead of Start?

options.text: When you need to reference other objects
For component initialization that doesn't depend on other objects
Awake and Start are the same

quizData.explanation: Awake runs first; ideal for self-setup.

slides.title: FixedUpdate() ⚙️
slides.content:
# Physics Time

`FixedUpdate()` is called on a regular timer, independent of frame rate. It's the place for **physics calculations** (moving Rigidbodies, applying forces).

- Default fixed timestep: 0.02 seconds (50 calls per second).
- Always use `FixedUpdate()` for `Rigidbody.MovePosition`, `AddForce`, etc.
- `Time.deltaTime` in FixedUpdate returns the fixed timestep automatically.

```csharp
void FixedUpdate()
{
    rb.AddForce(Vector3.forward * force);
}
```

quizData.question: Which method should you use for applying forces to a Rigidbody?
quizData.explanation: FixedUpdate syncs with the physics engine.

slides.title: Update() & LateUpdate() 🕒
slides.content:
# Frame-Rate Dependent Methods

- **Update()**: Called once per frame. Use for most game logic, input handling, non-physics movement.
- **LateUpdate()**: Called **after** all Update calls. Use for camera following, or any logic that depends on objects having moved in Update.

Typical order:
1. `Update()` – move player.
2. `LateUpdate()` – camera follows player.

```csharp
void LateUpdate()
{
    transform.position = target.position + offset;
}
```

slides.title: Other Event Methods 📋
slides.content:
# Useful Ones to Know

- `OnEnable()` / `OnDisable()` – called when the object is enabled/disabled.
- `OnCollisionEnter()`, `OnTriggerEnter()` – physics callbacks.
- `OnDestroy()` – when the object is destroyed.
- `OnMouseDown()` – when clicked (requires Collider).

All these are methods Unity looks for by name. No special registration needed.

slides.title: Lifecycle in Action
Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Execution Order Configuration

You can customize the order in which scripts' event methods run: **Edit → Project Settings → Script Execution Order**. This is useful when you need precise timing between different scripts.
